Task: Rate limiting + abuse controls on social exchange, guest lookup and magic-link endpoints (per IP and per identifier)

RateLimiting/AbuseLimits.cs holds every limit. THE LIMIT THAT PROTECTS BOOKINGS: per-REFERENCE failed lookups, 5 per 15 min from anywhere (checked before, counted after a failure, so correct lookups never count and a customer is never penalised). Also: per-IP on guest lookup/access, sign-in (and a separate failed-sign-in limit), refresh, service-token; send-link has a visible per-IP limit (429) and SILENT per-address and per-booking limits (202, nothing sent) so one mailbox cannot be flooded and existence cannot be probed. Client address: X-Forwarded-For is honoured ONLY from TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS (default loopback + RFC1918); an untrusted caller cannot dodge per-IP limits by forging it (tested). 25 tests; mutations of failure counting and the per-address limit were caught (the first attempt at the latter was not — my test reused one booking so another limit covered for it — so I added a test that isolates it). KNOWN TRADE-OFF: someone hammering a victim's reference can lock its SURNAME lookup for 15 min (the emailed link still works). REQUIRES: the storefront server must forward the client IP as X-Forwarded-For (P5). NOT COVERED: the AGENT login/verify/reset endpoints have no rate limit at all (see B-3).

Task: Customer token revocation (Redis jti set) checked on refresh and sensitive routes
Acceptance Criteria (how we know it's do: Logout/revoke makes refresh token unusable immediately
Notes: Done 2026-09-25 (completes the half started in P3-1). DESIGN CHANGE FOUND IN MY OWN P3-1 WORK: refresh-token revocation lived in Redis, which this stack runs with allkeys-lru — under memory pressure Redis can EVICT a 'this token was used' marker and a stolen refresh token would work again. Revocation is now DURABLE (Postgres table RevokedTokens; INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so exactly one caller wins). SESSIONS: every token in a sign-in chain shares a session id (sid); refreshing keeps it; signing out ends the whole session so the refresh token AND every access token of it die immediately, not after 15 minutes; other devices keep theirs. POST /api/v1/customers/me/logout-all sets Customer.TokensValidAfter so every session on every device ends; compared in MILLISECONDS (iat_ms claim) so signing straight back in within the same second works. Suspension and erasure take effect on the customer's next request. THE CHECK LIVES IN THE CustomerBearer SCHEME (runs on every customer request, explicit tenant because authentication precedes the tenant), so no future customer endpoint can forget it — proven by probing via logout-all, which does no checking of its own.
